title: NRI FCNR Deposits: Avoiding Currency Conversion Tax Errors
description: An NRI recently received relief from a ₹3.41 crore income tax addition due to a tax officer's currency conversion error. The officer mistakenly treated Japane.

faq.q: Are FCNR deposits taxable in India for NRIs?
faq.a: No, the interest earned on FCNR deposits is exempt from income tax in India for Non-Resident Indians.

faq.q: What is the difference between NRE and FCNR accounts?
faq.a: NRE (Non-Resident External) accounts are denominated in Indian Rupees, while FCNR (Foreign Currency Non-Resident) accounts are maintained in foreign currencies, protecting against exchange rate fluctuations. Both allow full repatriability of principal and interest.

faq.q: How can I prove the source of my FCNR funds to the tax authorities?
faq.a: You can prove the source by providing bank statements clearly showing the foreign currency, remittance proofs from your overseas bank, and documents like salary slips or business income statements from your country of residence.

faq.q: What should I do if a tax officer makes a currency conversion mistake in my assessment?
faq.a: You should immediately provide clear documentation to the assessing officer, highlighting the error. If not resolved at that stage, you can appeal the assessment to higher authorities like the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) or the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT).

faq.q: Can FCNR deposits be made in any foreign currency?
faq.a: No, FCNR deposits can only be made in designated foreign currencies approved by the RBI, which typically include USD, GBP, EUR, JPY, CAD, and AUD.

faq.q: Is the principal amount of FCNR deposits also tax-exempt?
faq.a: The principal amount of FCNR deposits is your own capital and is not considered income, so the question of it being "tax-exempt" doesn't apply in the same way as interest. The principal can be fully repatriated without tax implications.

faq.q: Do I need to declare my FCNR account in my Indian income tax return?
faq.a: While the interest income is exempt, it's generally good practice for NRIs to disclose all their Indian bank accounts, including FCNR accounts, in their income tax returns for transparency, even if the income is not taxable.

fact_check.summary: The article provides largely accurate information regarding FCNR deposits for NRIs, their tax treatment, and the importance of documentation, with most claims verified against authoritative sources.
